findings.explanation: The flagged line interpolates a request-derived value directly into a SQL string using % formatting: cursor.execute("DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE user_id = %s" % user_id). The value user_id comes from request.args.get("user_id", "") in the new run_maintenance() endpoint (PR diff, app/routes/admin.py), i.e. attacker-controlled query-string input. It is passed to cursor.execute() with no separate params argument, so the %s placeholder is never bound — the string is fully constructed before execution. This is a classic SQL injection sink. The @require_role("admin") decorator limits the attack surface to admin users but does not mitigate the injection (an admin can still inject arbitrary SQL, and the policy explicitly forbids this pattern). security-policy.md §5 states: 'All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters... String interpolation, f-strings, % formatting, .format(), or string concatenation of request-derived values into SQL is forbidden (CWE-89).' The code violates this directly. Note: the base branch (app/routes/admin.py lines 1-45) does not contain this endpoint — it is added by the PR — but the flagged line is the PR's new code, and the data flow (request.args -> % formatting -> cursor.execute) is fully confirmed from the diff.

evidence.content: cursor.execute("DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE user_id = %s" % user_id)

All SQL statements MUST use bound parameters (SQLAlchemy text() with :name parameters, or DB-API placeholders with a separate params argument). String interpolation, f-strings, % formatting, .format(), or string concatenation of request-derived values into SQL is forbidden (CWE-89).

findings.suggested_fix: Use a bound parameter instead of string interpolation: cursor.execute("DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE user_id = %s", (user_id,)). Additionally, validate that user_id is an integer (e.g., int(user_id)) before use, and prefer the SQLAlchemy ORM/session API (session.query(AuditLog).filter(AuditLog.user_id == user_id).delete()) over raw DB-API connections for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

findings.explanation: The new POST /maintenance endpoint is correctly protected against the authorization classes under review. The PR diff applies `@require_role("admin")` to `run_maintenance()`, which is the exact decorator mandated by security-policy.md §4 ('Every endpoint under /admin requires the admin role, enforced with @require_role("admin")') and api-spec.md ('/admin/maintenance | POST | admin only'). I verified in app/auth.py (lines 69-85) that `require_role` performs a real check: it resolves the bearer token via `get_current_user()`, returns 401 if absent, and 403 if `ROLE_RANK[user.role] < ROLE_RANK[minimum_role]` (admin=3). This is the sanctioned decorator, not a hand-rolled header check, so there is no CWE-862 (missing auth) or CWE-863 (incorrect/bypassable check). The endpoint does not fetch a user-owned object by a user-controlled identifier for read/update, so CWE-639 (IDOR) does not apply. Note: the diff does contain a separate SQL-injection flaw (CWE-89) via `"DELETE FROM audit_log WHERE user_id = %s" % user_id`, but that is outside the authorization scope of this review and is already flagged by the SAST finding.
